01 / What is confirmed — and proposed

What is confirmed — and proposed

Confirmed direction

A separate Noro-branded Shopify parts store for U.S. installers and machine builders. The existing Noro USA WordPress website stays in place.

Buyer priority

Material → diameter → category or part, with the technical detail needed to choose the right SKU. Parts enquiries should also lead to larger system-project conversations.

Recommendations for Mike’s approval

Public USD prices, guest checkout, the proposed family grouping, filter labels and theme selection. These are recommended store decisions, not additional requirements attributed to Mike.

Planning can proceed

The 2 November email confirms the team had enough information to start. Final prices, images and shipping inputs are due at the stages that need them.

02 / Compete on finding the right part

Compete on finding the right part

Mike’s commercial objective

Help Noro win U.S. parts business from established competitors, including Jacobs, while making system support easy to reach.

Relevant market reference

JACOB’s public site exposes product families, technical downloads, dimensional sheets, a CAD library and an online-order route.

Noro’s proposed response

Make material selection the main entry point. Keep both reducer ends, exact SKUs and source specifications visible. Preserve selections when buyers move between listings and products.

What we are not claiming

No measured conversion advantage, checkout superiority or cross-brand compatibility has been established. Jacobs-to-Noro matching remains later scope.

Market reference checked 10 November 2026: JACOB public site ↗. Noro recommendations are our interpretation, not a performance comparison.

06 / A concrete product-family proposal

A concrete product-family proposal

Proposed grouping

128 families, with a maximum of 140 SKUs in one family. Group by part name, material and descriptive design / finish. Keep elbow angle, construction, seal construction and with/without-seal differences separate.

Pipes

Diameter + wall thickness + length. Preserve only combinations present in the supplied product list; do not generate the full Cartesian product.

Reducers

Small-end diameter + large-end diameter + wall thickness. Both ends are parsed from each row’s description.

Other components

Diameter + source thickness / piping fit; length where relevant. Keep radius and design details as specifications. Connection assignments still require Noro review.

Offline check: all 2,287 SKUs retained; no duplicate option combinations within the proposed families. This is a proposed mapping, not a completed Shopify import.

08 / Navigation and filters

Navigation and filters

Primary discovery route

Shop by Material → diameter → category / part type. Keep category browsing and exact SKU search as alternative entry points.

Preserve the buyer’s context

Keep material and diameter when narrowing category, opening a product and returning to results. Seal links retain diameter but clear an incompatible metal filter.

Technical filters

Thickness / piping fit, length and angle where relevant. Reducers expose small-end and large-end diameter. Match every selected dimension to the same SKU.

Search and result counts

Use real SKU strings, including leading zeros. Distinguish product-family counts from matching SKU counts. No price sorting until approved USD prices exist.

Shopify Search & Discovery and theme filters are the intended implementation. Exact variant matching and SKU-to-variant landing need trial validation.

11 / Collection and product pages

Collection and product pages

Product listing

Show material, design detail, exact or example dimensions, and matching SKU count. Reducer cards always show both ends. “Choose exact part” leads to an existing SKU.

No misleading commercial data

The prototype shows “USD price pending” and does not convert EUR LIST into selling prices. No live-stock promise is inferred from the file.

Product detail

Expose SKU, material, description, diameter(s), thickness / fit, length, angle and original radius notation. Unprovided fields remain clearly unprovided.

Images and evidence

Use a static family image plus dimensional drawings / documents where available. Current schematics are labelled placeholders and do not prove compatibility.

12 / Image recommendation for Mike

Image recommendation for Mike

Coverage

Start with one consistent render per distinct geometry, material and construction. Add diameter-specific renders when proportions change visibly; compare an 80 mm and a 630 mm pipe before deciding coverage.

Format and resolution

Request square 2048 × 2048 px PNG masters; JPEG is suitable for opaque backgrounds. Use consistent angle, lighting and crop. Match files to a family / SKU list.

Using the existing 3D designs

Ask for representative CAD files and their formats. Validate an export-to-static-image workflow with Noro or a rendering specialist before estimating production effort.

Scope boundary

CRO Gurus recommends coverage and integrates supplied assets. CAD conversion, render production and interactive 3D are not established launch commitments; agree provider, cost and scope separately.

Mike raised the image questions on 2 November. The 3 November reply promises recommendations and notes additional research is needed. Image-format guidance: Shopify product media ↗.

13 / Cart, checkout and human enquiries

Cart, checkout and human enquiries

Proposed direct purchase

For launch-approved SKUs with approved USD price, saleable availability and supported shipping, show Add to Cart and use Shopify checkout. Public pricing and guest access need Mike’s approval.

Cart review

Keep exact SKU, both reducer ends, relevant dimensions and quantity visible. No assumed discount, currency conversion or duty calculation.

Human support

Carry the selected SKU and product reference into enquiries; request quantity and delivery ZIP when relevant. Larger projects have a clear enquiry route.

Exceptions require approved rules

Do not designate an entire regulator family as quote-only without Noro’s rule. No automated quote is promised. Final recipient and handling process are open.

15 / Shipping: approve the operating rules

Shipping: approve the operating rules

Established planning direction

Germany-to-U.S. fulfillment and a DHL-based approach were discussed. Final rates, service choices and exception rules are not established in the supplied evidence.

Inputs Noro must provide

Packed weights and dimensions, service coverage, rates, shipping origins, delivery wording, duties / handling terms and special-shipment rules.

CRO Gurus implementation

Configure and test the agreed shipping setup. Confirm standard-parcel and exception scenarios before live checkout testing.

Keep the implementation bounded

Weight bands are an option to evaluate, not an approved policy. Custom freight calculators, automatic landed-cost quotes and multi-carton logic beyond the agreed setup require separate scope.

The supplied product list has no weight or packaging fields. A correct product catalog alone cannot establish checkout shipping prices.

20 / Delivery stages and prerequisites

Delivery stages and prerequisites

PLANNING · ≈ 1 WEEK

Plan approval

Use the supplied product list and existing brief. Review structure, assumptions and real-product checks. Obtain store access for the theme trial. Mike approves the proposed approach.

DESIGN · ≈ 1 WEEK

Design approval

After plan approval: mobile and desktop homepage/navigation, listing and representative PDP. Use sufficient representative assets. One consolidated design revision round.

BUILD & LAUNCH · ≈ 2 WEEKS

Launch readiness

After design approval: implement, load approved assortment, test and launch. Requires final USD prices, stock process, shipping rules, assets, policies, payment and domain.

Stage estimates assume timely relevant inputs, payments and approvals. Final launch data is not a prerequisite to begin planning. No fixed launch date is committed.

21 / Launch boundary and support terms

Launch boundary and support terms

Launch scope

Focused parts discovery, agreed direct-purchase behavior, human enquiries, approved store implementation, app setup, testing and launch.

Later-phase ideas

System-project list uploads, AI-assisted quoting, Jacobs-to-Noro matching, configurators, automatic price/stock syncing and interactive 3D. Custom freight calculation is not a launch commitment.

Support terms to verify

The source summary flags a two-week versus six-week expiry conflict for unused support hours. This onboarding email PDF does not include the signed offer or resolve that conflict.

Before final contractual handoff

Check the signed offer and carry its support allowance and expiry into the agreed handoff. Do not substitute either unverified period.
